title: Cycle of Abuse
description: A predictable four-phase cycle: a build-up of tension, an acute abusive incident, a reconciliation phase, and a period of calm.

sections.title: What It Is
sections.content: A predictable four-phase cycle in many abusive relationships: a build-up of tension, an acute abusive incident, a reconciliation (honeymoon) phase, and a period of calm before tension builds again.

sections.title: How It Actually Appears
content: Tension phase: the abuser becomes increasingly irritable, critical, and on edge. The victim walks on eggshells, trying to prevent an explosion.
Explosion: abuse occurs—physical, verbal, or emotional—and the tension is released.
Reconciliation: the abuser apologizes profusely, cries, swears to change, gives gifts, and promises it will never happen again. The victim feels hope.
Calm: a period of relative peace follows, where the relationship seems normal or even wonderful, until tension begins creeping back.

sections.title: Common Behaviors
content: In tension phase: silent treatment, nitpicking, threats.
In explosion: explosive rage, cruelty, violence.
In reconciliation: charm, love bombing, victim-playing (“I’m a monster, I don’t deserve you”).
In calm: acting as if nothing happened, being the perfect partner.

sections.title: Real Phrases
content: “I promise it will be different this time.”
“I don’t know what came over me.”
“Look what you made me do.”
“I’ll kill myself if you leave.”

sections.title: Warning Signs
content: A repeating pattern: blow-up, apology, peace, blow-up.
You stay because of the wonderful calm phases, believing they are the “real” relationship.
The cycles are getting shorter and the abuse more severe.
You feel responsible for managing the abuser’s emotions to prevent an explosion.

sections.title: Why It Works
sections.content: The reconciliation phase provides massive emotional relief and dopamine, creating a trauma bond. The victim becomes conditioned to work harder to extend the calm phase, believing their behavior can control the abuser’s. This is classic intermittent reinforcement.

sections.title: Protection Strategy
content: Recognize the cycle and name it. Journal the phases so you can see the pattern objectively over time.
Understand that the calm phase is part of the abuse cycle, not a sign of recovery.
Develop a safety plan during the calm phase for when tension begins to rise again.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
content: Believing the abuser will change because they seem so sincere during reconciliation.
Thinking the cycle only applies to physical abuse; it occurs in emotional and verbal abuse too.

sections.title: Real Scenario
sections.content: Every few weeks, a husband’s criticism escalates into screaming, then into throwing objects. The next day, he brings flowers, cooks dinner, and is tender for a week. His wife lives for that week and endures the rest. After years, she realizes the weeks of peace have become days, and the explosions more frequent and worse.

sections.title: Key Insight
sections.content: The cycle of abuse is a wheel that only turns in one direction—toward more control. Peace bought by walking on eggshells isn’t peace; it’s the quiet before the next break.
